content:
Ever since iOS 5 in 2011, iPhones and iPads have come with a built-in Notification Center, which serves as a central place to check notifications from various apps in chronological order.

Starting from iOS 27, Apple has made a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 went through an entire summer of beta versions before its formal release. Between the first two betas, the relevant operation underwent minor changes. However, this change ultimately arrived with the official release, and I am still getting used to it.

Siri AI occupies most of the swipe gestures along the top edge of the iPhone and iPad.

On iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the default way to open Notification Center has not changed. However, enabling Siri AI simultaneously alters an important swipe gesture on iPhone and iPad.

After Siri AI is enabled, one way to summon it is to swipe down from the middle of the top edge of the iPhone or iPad screen. This gesture was previously used to open Notification Center.

Once Siri AI is enabled, users can still swipe down from the top-left corner of the screen to open Notification Center. Notifications now slide in from the top-left corner with animation. This change appears to be directing users' attention to the reduced touch area for Notification Center.

Apple has greatly prioritized access to Siri AI in iOS 27. Most of the top edge area is used to summon the all-new Siri experience.

The last time Apple modified how Notification Center is opened was when the iPhone X moved Control Center from a swipe up from the bottom to a swipe down from the top-right corner. Apple later unified this operational experience across the platform.

Notifications have now moved to the top-left corner

Now it is Notification Center's turn to be relegated to the corner. Especially in iPadOS 27 beta 1, almost the entire area above the app icons at the top of the home screen is used to summon Siri AI. If users turn off displaying AM/PM or the date, the actual area for opening Notification Center shrinks even further.

Top comment posted by mz4srmsr

I've always swiped down from the top-left corner to view notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the middle to open Notification Center 😂 So I should be fine, right?

Apple improved this in iPadOS 27 beta 2, making the left and right sides form more unified areas. The size is roughly equal to the width of two app columns, with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right, while the rest is used to summon Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it does take some time to judge whether this change is worthwhile or worth reconsidering. At the same time, based on initial reactions, the market response to Apple's new Siri AI system has been generally very positive. Hearing the phrase "Siri is finally useful," I think everyone also needs time to adjust.

After months of continued use of this new operation, if I could turn it off, I definitely would. Since there is currently no option to disable the gesture of swiping down from the middle of the top to summon Siri, the only thing I can do is build new muscle memory and avoid swiping from the middle.

What do you think? If you could choose, would you revert to the old settings? Is this change of using a swipe gesture to summon Siri worthwhile? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
